newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates ease to 3.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates ease to 3.05 pct.

text.p: German call money rates eased to around 3.05 percent on Wednesday from 3.05 to 3.10 percent on Tuesday as the market recovered from the end-of-month liquidity squeeze.
"The market seems to have weathered the end-of-month deadline relatively quickly," said a dealer.
"We are looking quite good in terms of reserves. Therefore I can see call money rates more around 3.00 to 3.05 percent in the near future than 3.05 to 3.10 percent," he added.
The market was unperturbed by the Bundesbank's 2.1 billion mark funds drain in its weekly tender, dealers said.
In fact the drain ought to help normalise the high level of reserves currently held, dealers said.
The Bundesbank allocated 78.9 billion marks in securities repurchase funds on Wednesday, replacing a repo pact for 81 billion marks.
Daily reserves held by commercial banks at the Bundesbank fell to 46.1 billion marks on Tuesday from 57.3 billion on Monday and the monthly average rose to 46.1 billion from 41.4 billion.
Borrowings at the Lombard window were negligible at 100 million marks, down from 14.5 billion on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= rate was quoted at 3.07800 percent on Wednesday, down from 3.09467 percent on Tuesday.
